prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Warehouse boundary: receiving to outbound load release. Elements: Inbound Inspection Desk (Cinderbay): checks paperwork/trailer ID/seals, records damage and inspection outcomes before routine handling; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note to Yard Gate Controller. Pallet Dimension Scanner (Moonquarry): measures pallets for alternate paths; produces Oversize Load Advisory, which never authorizes rule-failing placement. Inbound Pallet Buffer: staging when not ready. North/South Aisle Stacker Cranes report availability; North (Juniperwake) sends Aisle Occupancy Snapshot on change. East/West Transfer Conveyors: separate routes to outbound staging. Conveyor Line Controller (Brasshaven): sequences, stops on downstream hazards; produces Transfer Induction Ticket per induction. Autonomous Forklift Fleet (Larkspur): produces Forklift Handoff Confirmation (vehicle/pallet ID, time, deferred moves). Yard Gate Controller (Velvetrook): validates arrivals, assigns lane/door, flags unscheduled, records discrepancies, holds risky vehicles. Outbound Dispatch Sorter: receives Dispatch Wave Amendment. Outbound Checkweigh Scale: verifies weight before shipping record finalized. Shipping Documentation Desk: records from confirmed data. Safety Zone Controller, Fire Alarm Panel: stop/restrict movement; Panel produces Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice. Maintenance Release Terminal (Copperfield): produces Crane Service Release Card after maintenance checks. Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (exceptions, holds, defers conflicted work, reviews delays/stops/staging before wave release); drivers, receiving, yard staff. Warehouse Management System (Morrowglass): authoritative task/inventory state; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment on post-prep changes; produces Slot Reservation Receipt. Requirements: valid receipt instruction; door only when door/lane/crew free; count before unloading done; segregate damage; exceptions visible to supervisor until resolved; traceable holds; attribute mismatch blocks auto-allocation, routes to review; record scan result/location/time; cranes in authorized zones; conveyor entry after inspection; interlocks; blocked transfer holds upstream; single merges; duplicate tickets held; stale snapshot holds path; order-preserving resume; no move without WMS release; maintenance authorization before return to service; sorter keeps order unless amended, verifies staging; forklifts need valid status/route/destination, confirm pallet ID before lifting, stop when safety blocks; work requests need unique reference, destination, constraints.

New part:
S151: Cinderbay consumes its inspection-stage advisory and records whether the pallet can proceed, requires rework, or must remain held.
S152: A held pallet remains separated from available stock until the review outcome is entered and validated.
S153: Inbound Pallet Buffer provides temporary staging without implying that a held load has been accepted into inventory.
S154: North Aisle Stacker Crane uses the Slot Reservation Receipt to confirm that its assigned destination remains reserved.
S155: Before movement, the crane checks its current task state and stops if the destination or access path is no longer valid.
S156: Morrowglass, the Warehouse Management System, consumes the load advisory to apply the required handling constraints to affected work.
S157: The system prevents an incompatible allocation from being released while the advisory remains applicable.
S158: If a task is blocked, the control record identifies the hold reason and retains the pallet's last confirmed location.
S159: Warehouse Operations Supervisor reviews unresolved holds and assigns an escalation when the operating team cannot clear them locally.
S160: The supervisor also confirms that a delayed task will not compromise a later outbound wave or an aisle access limit.
S161: Service readiness requires a recorded fault state, a controlled work area, and a clear separation between maintenance activity and live movement.
S162: North Aisle Stacker Crane reports a fault that could affect positioning, load retention, braking, or travel before the equipment is returned to service.
S163: The affected crane remains unavailable while personnel inspect the fault and verify that adjacent equipment can continue safely.
S164: Maintenance Release Terminal records the inspection outcome and the identity of the person authorizing a return to operation.
S165: A failed test keeps the equipment inhibited and returns the fault to the maintenance queue for further diagnosis.
S166: A successful test does not by itself release the crane until required interlocks and operating limits have been checked.
S167: Outbound Checkweigh Scale produces the Gross Weight Variance Slip when a measured pallet weight falls outside the configured tolerance.
S168: The variance remains unresolved until the pallet is reweighed or the documented review establishes a safe disposition.
S169: Conveyor Line Controller holds affected transfers when an exception would make the next movement uncertain.
S170: Fire Alarm Panel and Safety Zone Controller retain authority to stop or restrict movement whenever their safety status requires it.
S171: Warehouse Operations Supervisor releases normal work only after outstanding exceptions, maintenance holds, and access constraints have been reconciled.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
